title: Vibe Coding at Scale: Customizing AI Assistants for Enterprise Environments - Harald Kirshner,
talk_summary: A VS Code team demo of 'vibe coding' maturity levels (YOLO → structured → spec-driven), showing how templates, custom chat modes, instruction files, prompts, and MCP tools constrain an agent to house conventions.

takeaways.technique: Mode-scoped agent definitions (system prompt + allowed tools per mode)
takeaways.what_they_do: Define named chat modes in a repo folder, each bundling a system prompt and a specific tool set, so switching mode changes both behavior and capabilities (e.g. a TDD mode that must write tests first and stop for review).
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can define already tools. You'd find what what tools are in the mode and what's the system prompt

takeaways.what_they_do: Instruction files describe what specific parts of the codebase do and are made dynamic per area, so the agent gets local conventions only where relevant.
takeaways.evidence_quote: instructions. Those are new. Those are githubinstructions. And those can outline what specific parts of the codebase do

takeaways.technique: Feed linter/task-runner diagnostics back into the agent loop
takeaways.what_they_do: Wire VS Code problems/tasks so the agent sees lint and task errors as it works and fixes its own mistakes before handing off.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you have your task runners set up in VS Code and your llinters properly, it will actually start fixing code as it makes mistakes

takeaways.technique: Test-first mode with a mandatory human/agent review checkpoint
takeaways.what_they_do: A TDD mode forces tests to be written and passing before implementation, and pauses for confirmation after tests so the tests can be reviewed before code is written.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you have to write tests first and then you write code and it has to pass and only ask only move to writing code after I confirm

takeaways.what_they_do: Commit working code frequently and pause the agent to inspect, so regressions are localized and recoverable rather than discovered after a long run.
takeaways.evidence_quote: keep committing the that workable code so you don't get into weird areas where it worked before and now my VIP coding broke it

takeaways.technique: Template repo with pinned stack and conventions
takeaways.what_they_do: Start projects from an internal template that fixes the tech stack and ships instructions steering the agent to house conventions (e.g. Fluent UI), instead of letting the model pick frameworks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: because it's a template It comes with this consistent text stack and it comes with instructions to guide uh the copilot flow onto a specific conventions
